author_proof_steps.action: Form the block-diagonal hard Gaussian family using independent same-sign orthogonal blocks and an identity remainder.
Identify the actual prior-averaged target with the product of the single-block mixtures and the independent standard Gaussian remainder; omit the latter if kn=d.
Use Lebesgue densities of those actual measures and Eq6 to write the high-dimensional product density in block coordinates.
Apply Tonelli to the nonnegative square-root product, extract k identical affinity factors, and use the remainder Gaussian integral one.
Handle kn=d by the same factorization with the remainder factor omitted.
Use probability density normalization for TV=1-integral min; apply pointwise min(u,v)<=sqrt(uv) and Ex71 to obtain TV>=1-a^k.
Apply the previously derived single-block affinity upper bound and raise it to k to obtain the amplified quantitative lower bound.

D_b is a law of actual block precision matrices, not a freely chosen probability measure with a stipulated product property.
